title: Sucuklu yumurta
subtitle: Fried eggs with Turkish sucuk sausage
excerpt: Sucuk is a dry, heavily spiced Turkish beef sausage that sizzles in its own fat and infuses everything around it with deep paprika warmth. Eggs fried in the rendered fat are the simplest and best pairing. This is a two-ingredient breakfast that tastes of somewhere very specific.
sourceNotes: A staple of the Turkish kahvalti (breakfast spread), sucuklu yumurta appears in homes, lokantas, and roadside cafes across Turkey.

content.text: Sucuk is a garlic-and-paprika-spiked dried beef sausage that is one of the defining flavours of the Turkish breakfast. It needs no oil; it fries in its own fat, which turns a deep brick-red and smells extraordinary.
The eggs go into that fat and pick up the spiced, smoky flavour as they set. The result is a plate that is deeply savoury, a little fatty in the best possible way, and gone very quickly.

Sucuk is available in Turkish and Middle Eastern food shops and some supermarkets. If you cannot find it, merguez makes a decent substitute, though the spice profile is different. Use a heavy pan; the sausage catches quickly in a thin one.

items.prepNote: or Turkish sucuk sausage, sliced into 1 cm rounds

content.text: Place the sliced sausage in a cold frying pan, then set it over a medium heat. As the pan warms, the fat will begin to render. Fry the sausage for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until both sides are browned and the fat in the pan is red and fragrant.

Push the sausage slices to the edges of the pan. Crack the eggs into the centre, into the fat. Cook over a medium heat until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny, about 3 minutes. Spoon some of the red fat over the whites as they cook. Scatter aleppo pepper and parsley over the top. Serve straight from the pan with bread.

items.symptom: Sausage burnt before eggs are cooked
items.cause: Pan too hot or sausage sliced too thin
items.fix: Use medium rather than high heat. Slice the sausage at least 1 cm thick so it holds together.

items.cause: Not enough fat or pan not hot enough
items.fix: Make sure the sausage renders enough fat first. If the pan looks dry, add a splash of olive oil before the eggs.

items.cause: Left too long in residual heat
items.fix: Serve immediately off the heat; the pan stays very hot.

content.text: Add a handful of chopped peppers to the pan after the sausage and let them soften in the fat before adding the eggs. This moves it towards a light menemen. Some cooks crack the eggs over the sausage without pushing them aside; the yolks sit on top of the slices and the whole thing bakes together.
This is best cooked and eaten immediately. The sausage can be sliced ahead and kept in the fridge.

Sucuklu yumurta is part of the Turkish kahvalti, a leisurely spread that can include 20 or more small dishes. It also appears as a quick supper or a restorative lunch. The combination of cured meat and egg appears across the region in different forms, but the sucuk version is distinctly Turkish.
